runners_data.name: C Pas Possible
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old with one placed run on identical Good ground at this sort of trip; style unknown — Andrew Kinirons stable is 1/3 in 14 days, and 52 days off is manageable, but limited profile makes assessment difficult.

runners_data.name: Dad Sez
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott yard and Jack Kennedy is a powerhouse booking for an unexposed six-year-old who fell on his only hurdles start; going profile completely unknown but connections alone demand respect, and 81 days off is not a concern for this stable.

runners_data.name: De Jour En Jour
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer on Good ground over this range of trips, making him the most reliable prominent runner in the field; Ross O'Sullivan stable is quiet (0/12 in 14 days) but De Jour En Jour's form figures of 3-2-2-3 show relentless honesty and the trip suits.

runners_data.name: Eternal Reward
runners_data.note: Hold-up type flagged as a fader in the finish, which is a concern in a marathon maiden over 2m6f; has been off 297 days since a modest run at Headford and the Margaret Mullins stable is 0/3 in 14 days — plenty stacked against.

runners_data.name: Excessivebehaviour
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type who fades late, returning after 248 days on the easy side of his form — one flat run over 22f on Yielding is thin evidence, and Martin Brassil is 0/0 in 14 days; needs everything to fall right.

runners_data.name: Frankie's Freebie
runners_data.note: Busy recent campaign (23 days since last run) and consistent placed form on Good ground over shorter trips; Harry Sexton (7) is an apprentice in a big field, which adds positional risk, but the horse's natural prominence and form over Good ground make it a genuine mid-market contender.

runners_data.name: I Can Find Em
runners_data.note: Unknown going profile and lightly raced, but has placed form from hurdles including a second and two thirds; amateur jockey Mr O McGill (5) and a quiet stable (0/0 in 14 days) are negatives in a competitive field.

runners_data.name: Jeroboam Machin
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter, labelled with a style-fit caution (0.90) because his best form came over shorter on Soft/Heavy; the two Good-ground runs over this sort of trip produced a third and fourth, suggesting he may set the table rather than win it.

runners_data.name: Killowen House
runners_data.note: Placed twice on Good ground at this trip and undeniably course-relevant, but his natural hold-up style means he is squeezed into a midfield position in this shape — he cannot operate from his preferred deep-cover berth in a 21-runner field with this configuration, which is a meaningful handicap on his true chance.

runners_data.name: Kiltinan
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a single hurdles run (fourth) and 241 days off the track; style and going profile both unknown, and an amateur jockey in a wide-open 21-runner maiden is a challenging context for a horse with so little evidence.

runners_data.name: Minella Post
runners_data.note: Tumbled form figures including a fall last time and a string of midfield finishes; best effort was a fourth over 24f on Soft which is some distance from his 5/7 strike-rate on Good — James Smith (5) has a tough task.

runners_data.name: Mr Erwitt
runners_data.note: Poor recent form (P-P-P in his last three) and a going-OK flag that flatters his profile; a genuine hold-up type whose position has been remapped inward because the back of this field is already congested, so he will not find the cover he needs and his fade-prone finishing style compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Mr Hollywood
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins' hold-up type has placed in five of his last five races on mixed ground, including two thirds on Good; Brian Hayes is a strong booking and the yard is 5/27 in 14 days — the concern is that a steady pace from Jeroboam Machin may not produce the gap a hold-up horse needs over 2m6f.

runners_data.name: Ol Parson
runners_data.note: Moderate form including a PU and several mid-pack finishes; two runs on Good ground produced a sixth and ninth, and a 23-day turnaround with a 7lb claimer is not an obvious formula for improvement.

runners_data.name: Rumi Rock
runners_data.note: Ran just eight days ago which needs monitoring for freshness; two runs on Good ground both resulted in mid-pack finishes (sixth, tenth) and Phillip Enright is a capable conditional, but the form profile is uninspiring for this mark.

runners_data.name: Tom Mac
runners_data.note: Single hurdles run six months ago (sixth over 23f on Good) and style unknown; the Paul O'Flynn stable is 0/0 in 14 days and Darragh O'Keeffe's booking is the strongest asset on limited evidence.

runners_data.name: Trotters Traders
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who fades in the finish and has only one run — a distant sixteenth on Good ground over a shorter trip; Paul John Gilligan is 0/6 in 14 days and this horse is 0/1 lifetime in a notoriously difficult discipline for faders.

runners_data.name: Trev The Rev
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a single pulled-up run on Soft and 120 days off; the lightest weight (161lbs) is a small positive, but an unknown going profile and very limited form evidence makes this a significant risk in a 21-runner field — the Gilligan stable is 0/6 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Al Arrivee
runners_data.note: The form standout on raw figures — two wins on Good ground, all five hurdles runs placed or better, trained by Willie Mullins and ridden by Patrick Mullins; the yard is 5/27 in 14 days and the step up from 18f to 22f on Good ground appears straightforwardly within range.

runners_data.name: Shoda
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's 1/67 14-day strike rate is significant context; Shoda has one win and four places from five starts including a win on Soft, and the step from 18f to 22f is his big question — J J Slevin is an elite booking that keeps him firmly on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Walkingmayotomilan
runners_data.note: Returns after 185 days with no jockey listed in the data, which is a notable negative flag; hold-up style that fades late, with poor form (2-3-2-P-0 in recent starts) and a previous run on Heavy that was unsatisfactory — very hard to recommend.

races.paceDynamic: Jeroboam Machin is the confirmed front-runner and, in a 21-runner maiden hurdle over 2m6f on Good ground, is likely to set a measured, sustainable gallop from the front without being seriously pressured for the lead. Al Arrivee and De Jour En Jour will push to sit prominently just behind, while Shoda and Frankie's Freebie fill out the chasing pack, meaning there is a genuine cluster of prominent-minded horses who will be eyeing the same early positions. The field contains more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Killowen House and Mr Erwitt are true hold-up horses remapped to midfield, meaning the genuine closers' berths are contested and those two will not find their natural position. A steady-to-fair pace set by one lone front-runner over this extended trip on Good ground historically suits prominent racers who travel smoothly and avoid trouble; horses able to sit second or third without burning fuel early will be best placed to pounce from the second-last, making the prominent-to-midfield profile the primary beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jeroboam Machin Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Jeroboam Machin leads unchallenged and the pace proves steady enough for a prominent chaser to pounce at the second-last.
scenarios.body: Jeroboam Machin sets a comfortable tempo and the race is run to suit horses who travel prominently just off the lead, with Al Arrivee and De Jour En Jour ideally positioned to strike turning for home; the Good ground rewards those who save energy rather than grinding from the back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens enough in the final mile to stretch the field and create a genuine closing opportunity from off the pace.
scenarios.body: A faster mid-race tempo would string out the field over the 2m6f trip, leaving a genuine gap for a fresh-legged closer to pick off tired front-runners approaching the last; Mr Hollywood from the Willie Mullins yard is the obvious profile beneficiary, though Killowen House — a true hold-up type squeezed toward midfield — could also land late if the pace honestly tests stamina.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Battles
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent horses push for position early and the resulting contested pace sets up a stamina test from three out.
scenarios.body: Al Arrivee, De Jour En Jour and Frankie's Freebie all pressing forward would lift the tempo and turn this into a thorough stamina examination, favouring horses with the deepest reserves of staying power over the final two flights; De Jour En Jour's consistent placed form at this sort of trip on Good ground makes it the ideal profile, while Shoda's yard form (Joseph O'Brien, 16/67 in 14 days) adds weight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Surprise — Lightly Raced
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unexposed or unknown-quantity runners outclasses the field on debut or near-debut form that has been underestimated.
scenarios.body: With several lightly raced or unknown-style horses (Dad Sez with Jack Kennedy, Kiltinan, Tom Mac, Trev The Rev) lurking at long odds, a single sharp performance from an unexposed type could render the pace map redundant; Dad Sez in particular carries the significant advantage of Jack Kennedy and the Gordon Elliott yard despite an unknown going profile, making it the standout from this group.

watchPoints.text: Al Arrivee and Mr Hollywood represent Willie Mullins with two strong pilots — watch for any market move that suggests the stable has a preference, as it could identify the intended runner in the most powerful yard in the race.

Jeroboam Machin's front-running role is confirmed but his style-fit flag and modest recent Good-ground form (third, fourth) suggest he is vulnerable to being passed before the last — watch whether he is allowed to bowl along solo or if Al Arrivee or De Jour En Jour press him early.

Killowen House and Mr Erwitt are both genuine hold-up types displaced inward by the sheer volume of closers in this field — if the pace is slow early, neither will find the ground they need to deliver their run, and they should be downgraded accordingly in-running.

Dad Sez (Jack Kennedy, Gordon Elliott) is unknown on going and lightly raced but the form of the booking is impossible to ignore in a wide-open maiden — watch for any market support that suggests stable confidence following the stable's 4/30 recent form.

With 21 runners over 2m6f on Good ground, positional chaos in the early stages is likely — horses drawn wide or slow to jump the first flight could lose significant ground before the pace settles, making early jumping sharpness a key watch point across the field.

runners_data.name: Hees Dynamite
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who set sensible fractions on recent good-ground starts; uncontested lead is a major tactical asset but the lone-leader role under a 5lb claimer in a 23-runner field brings stamina questions at 2m6f on only 12 days' rest.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out, with wins three and four starts back, but he's only 18th of 23 on our rating; he has raced over today's trip and going before, 12 days after his latest run.

runners_data.name: Harbour Highway
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type wearing tongue-tie whose best form comes on good ground; Harry Cobden's big-field race-management is a clear positive, and two placed efforts at 2m4f+ on good ground underline the staying credentials needed here.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up placings in his last five starts underline the ability, and fifth of 23 on our rating is more than enough claim, even with a below-par effort when pulled up last time out; he has also raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Mephisto
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent performer who handles good going well (12/15 sim-going score) but the tongue-tie and visor combo can indicate a horse needing holding together; shorter trip form in recent history is a mild concern over 2m6f in such a large field.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, fourth two starts back, but a winner five starts back, and a rating of 109 puts him 12th of 23; he has raced over today's trip and going before, 15 days after his latest run.

runners_data.name: Oneforgonzo
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on good ground and placed over further, so the trip is fine; tongue-tie noted, and 69 days off the track plus a 7lb amateur claim is a significant combination to overcome in a 23-runner competitive handicap.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out but a winner two starts back, this gelding is workmanlike rather than progressive at 17th of 23 on our rating, and a 69-day absence adds to the doubts; he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Granville Street
runners_data.note: Prominent-style horse whose form has been exclusively at much shorter trips (12-16f) in recent runs — today's 2m6f is an unproven stamina test and the drop back to Good from those recent Flat-style distances raises legitimate questions.
runners_data.comment: Yet to feature at the finish in his last four starts, but a rating of 110 for ninth of 23 suggests capable form is still there; he has raced over today's going before following a 33-day break.

runners_data.name: Ollie La Ba Ba
runners_data.note: Has tongue-tie, prominent style, and solid good-ground record (11/15); the winning form over 18f at this grade is encouraging but the horse has placed only once in six runs since that win, suggesting a horse that needs things to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Four sixths bookending a win four starts back make the form hard to fathom, though a rating of 111 for eighth of 23 keeps him competitive; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 51 days off.

runners_data.name: Camino Rock
runners_data.note: 188-day layoff is a serious fitness flag for a nine-year-old whose recent form has been all question marks at Healey's; the single good-ground run in recent history (9th over 16f) offers little encouragement for this extended trip.
runners_data.comment: Highly regarded on our figures, this gelding ranks third of 23 with a rating of 115, but the recent form is concerning - unseated, pulled up twice and two ninths in his last five - and he returns from a 188-day absence.

runners_data.name: Coded Welder
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie, two recent placed efforts on good ground including a second over 19f, and the horse appears to be building — the 0W5P record in similar conditions is a minor negative but the form trend is upward.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, and runner-up two starts back, this gelding has been competitive without getting his head in front, and a rating of 115 for fourth of 23 rates him highly; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 54 days off.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Won impressively over 2m on good ground just five days ago under Sam Ewing and the Noel Meade team has had 3 winners from 12 in the past 14 days; the 26f run (4th) shows the horse stays, but the quick turnaround is the key risk.
runners_data.comment: A win last time out is the standout, but modest efforts before that - fourth, sixth, ninth and sixth in the four runs prior - explain a rating of just 108 for 14th of 23; he has raced over today's going before, quick to reappear just five days on.

runners_data.name: I'll Be Handy
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in the finish and the hold-up flag reflects that — in a 23-runner field over 2m6f, a horse that fades late is a structural problem; the four-year-old has placed twice over shorter trips but the flagged stamina concern at this distance is real.
runners_data.comment: Two runner-up efforts three and four starts back show ability, but an eighth last time out and a rating of just 105 for 20th of 23 make this a hard sell; he has raced over today's going before but is 68 days removed from that last run.

runners_data.name: Lord Ffrench
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with tongue-tie who has struggled to win in nine good-ground runs but placed twice; the 52-day break and consistent midfield finishes over 19-22f suggest a horse that runs its race without threatening.
runners_data.comment: A win five starts back is now some way behind a run of modest finishes since, and a rating of 106 for 19th of 23 reflects that decline; he has raced over today's going before after a 52-day break.

runners_data.name: Imarajan
runners_data.note: Strong recent profile — won over 18f and second over 19f both on good ground — and the 7lb claimer Paddy Cody adds intrigue; the horse's 1W5P sim-going record and upward trajectory make this one of the better unexposed profiles in the field.
runners_data.comment: A win last time out, and a runner-up spot two starts back, mark this out as in-form, though a rating of just 104 leaves him 21st of 23 here; he has raced over today's going before, 19 days on from that latest win.

runners_data.name: Andys Flame
runners_data.note: Natural prominent racer who rode to a third over 19f on good going last time; the redistribution to midfield in this field shape means Shane Fitzsimons faces an awkward early traffic problem, and the STYLE_FIT discount is justified given the pack of prominent types ahead of this horse in the pecking order.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, this gelding looks capable of running well again on a rating of 116 that puts him second of 23, though he returns for a yard currently winless with its last 24 runners in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Cornmarket
runners_data.note: Three wins on good ground over 26f is excellent trip and going profile for today; Alan King (7lb claimer) takes the mount and while the horse's true style is prominent, it is one of the better-credentialed horses forced into a compromised position by the overcrowded front end.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out is a step forward, though a fall three starts back and a rating of just 104 for 22nd of 23 temper the enthusiasm; a winner four starts back, and he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Paul Collins
runners_data.note: Third over 24f on good ground most recently and the trip clearly suits; this is a horse that races prominently and the early scrimmage in a 23-runner field could prove costly, but Darragh O'Keeffe's tactical nous in big fields is a genuine positive.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out is the highlight of a modest recent sequence, and a rating of 110 for 10th of 23 rates him more highly than the bare form suggests; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 23 days off.

runners_data.name: Tangara Bay
runners_data.note: Won last start over 19f on soft — the switch to good ground here on 125 days off the track is a significant double query; just 1 from 5 on similar going and the only win in recent history came on softer.
runners_data.comment: A win last time out catches the eye, but that was 125 days ago and a rating of just 104 leaves her bottom of the 23 here; she has raced over today's going before but the layoff is a concern.

runners_data.name: Lucy Wang
runners_data.note: Three course wins at 24f on good going is an appealing profile but the 114-day layoff and the fact that her natural prominent style will be squeezed by this large field are both negatives; Donagh Meyler is capable but the redistribution into a midfield slot works against her.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out continues a consistent record that also includes wins two and five starts back, and a rating of 108 for 16th of 23 looks fair; she has raced over today's going before, despite having been off the track for 114 days.

runners_data.name: Mighty Berkshire
runners_data.note: Amateur jockey, tongue-tie and hood combination, 59 days off the track, and a 0W in seven runs on similar going — the profile does not scream competitive threat, though the horse has run creditably over 19-25f in good ground company before.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out is respectable enough, and a rating of 111 for seventh of 23 marks him out as better than his official mark suggests; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 59 days off.

runners_data.name: Therellbguddaysyet
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old whose natural prominent style will be crowded out early; the STYLE_FIT tag is apt — the horse has form at this sort of trip and going but at this age, being forced to race out of style in a field this size is a meaningful structural disadvantage.
runners_data.comment: He sits highest of the 23 runners on our figures, a rating of 118 that puts him narrowly ahead, though pulled up last time out and modest form before that - eighth, fifth and fourth - are the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Macshadow Des Crai
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy is a significant jockey booking for a horse on a 122-day absence; the form is at shorter trips on softer ground than today (just 1/4 on similar going) so the step up in distance and faster ground both need to be taken on trust.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up two starts back is the standout form, though a seventh last time out and a lengthy 122-day absence temper things; a rating of 109 for 13th of 23 rates him fairly, and he has raced over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Clonbury Bridge
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old with solid good-ground form (13/15 sim-going score) and has placed in similar handicaps; the natural prominent style is squeezed by the big field, the tongue-tie and visor are habitual, and no jockey is listed which is an unusual practical note.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up four starts back shows the ability, but two efforts pulled up in his last five starts and a 65-day absence are the concerns; a rating of 112 for sixth of 23 keeps faith, and he has raced over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Priory Park
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old whose recent form includes a 9th and a string of unplaced efforts; while the horse stays this trip and acts on good ground, form figures of 504P9 represent a horse that has been consistently below par and redistribution into midfield makes things harder still.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent sequence, capped by a ninth last time out, offers little encouragement, though a rating of 108 for 15th of 23 is fair; he has raced over today's trip and going before after 102 days off.

runners_data.name: Mavetherave
runners_data.note: Last run was an 8th over 24f on good ground — the worst recent form — and the horse has 0 wins and just 2 places in nine similar-going runs; a six-year-old that should be improving but isn't showing it.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up five starts back shows some ability, but an eighth last time out and a moderate run of finishes since keep him hovering at 11th of 23 on our rating; he has raced over today's trip and going before, 25 days after that latest run.

races.paceDynamic: Hees Dynamite is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 23-runner field and, with no serious challenger for the lead, should settle into a relaxed, owner-dictated rhythm from the front — creating a genuinely sustainable gallop rather than a searingly fast pace. Good ground at Galway over 2m6f will reward those who travel well through the race and pick up from a position of comfort. The field is notably overloaded with prominent types — Cornmarket, Andys Flame, Therellbguddaysyet, Lucy Wang, Clonbury Bridge, Mavetherave, Priory Park, and Mephisto among others all want to race close to the pace but cannot all secure their natural positions in a field of 23; of those, Mephisto, Oneforgonzo, and Paul Collins are the likeliest to physically get close to the front given their draw and profile, while the rest will be compromised and effectively racing from midfield. With one genuine leader, a controlled pace, and a large field funnelling runners into mid-division through no tactical choice, this race shape strongly favours genuine hold-up horses and any stalker who can track from a comfortable second-flight position without burning energy in a scrimmage — closers with proven good-ground form over this sort of trip are structurally advantaged.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Closers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Hees Dynamite bowls along unchallenged at a steady clip and the congested midfield fails to string the race out early.
scenarios.body: Hees Dynamite sets a fair but unpressured tempo, the large field compresses into a bunch through the early stages, and the race only truly ignites from the home turn; hold-up horses with the class to pick through traffic on good ground come to the fore in the final two flights. True hold-up runners who handle good going and have the stamina for 2m6f are best placed to capitalise as the pace quickens late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Stalker Picks Off Leader
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent horse sits a length or two off Hees Dynamite throughout and simply outstays the leader from the second-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: The pace is comfortable enough that a horse travelling well in second or third can shadow the leader without being exposed, then produce a clean jump at the last two flights to assert; this suits a prominent type with genuine stamina who avoids the early scrimmage. Mephisto and Imarajan are the best-placed prominent runners to actually secure that position and execute the plan.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Passes Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Hees Dynamite's steady front-running pace suddenly fades in the final half-mile and a wall of horses sweeps past.
scenarios.body: A hot gallop is unlikely given the sole front-runner, but if Hees Dynamite is not travelling within herself late, the good ground allows the entire mid-pack to quicken simultaneously and swamp the leaders; horses with a strong finish and held up early become the main beneficiaries. Golden Temple's recent form and Harbour Highway's hold-up profile suit this perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Types Cause Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the many displaced prominent types push forward early and create an unexpectedly strong early pace that fragments the field.
scenarios.body: If several of the overloaded prominent horses — Cornmarket, Andys Flame, Therellbguddaysyet — refuse their mapped midfield role and crowd the early stages, it turns into a true test of stamina and cuts the field down to the pure stayers; however, given each carries a STYLE_FIT discount and most are on OR 103-105, the likelihood of them engineering a winning advantage is low. Cornmarket and Andys Flame are the most likely to benefit if this chaos does materialise given their distance form.

watchPoints.text: Golden Temple ran just five days ago and won well under Sam Ewing — watch for how fresh the horse looks in the parade ring, as a quick turnaround at Galway can expose fitness issues mid-race despite the winning momentum.

The large group of redistributed prominent types (Cornmarket, Andys Flame, Therellbguddaysyet, Lucy Wang, Clonbury Bridge) all want the front end — watch the first two flights for crowding and potential interference as they funnel into a single-file position that physically cannot accommodate them all.

Hees Dynamite is the only confirmed front-runner but is ridden by a 5lb claimer in a field of 23 — if Patrick M O'Brien loses control of the pace at any point, the race shape transforms entirely and hold-up horses gain an even stronger positional advantage.

I'll Be Handy carries a flagged tendency to fade in the finish at 2m6f — if backed in the market, the race distance and the holding-up style make this horse a structural risk for those looking for finishing runners.

runners_data.name: She's A Fine Wine
runners_data.note: OR 125 and the race's sole confirmed front-runner; De Bromhead in form (6/39 T14), two wins from last two over Good ground — she dictates here on a Good surface that suits her 11/15 similar-going record.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and again two starts back, She's A Fine Wine brings the stronger form into this line-up and has run over today's trip and going before; a below-par ninth three starts back is the only blot.

runners_data.name: Venusienne
runners_data.note: Mullins-Cobden combination (5/27 T14) gives this one serious claims; the mare showed her best form at Galway (3rd and 1st in Good) and her prominent style should see her within striking range of the leader.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a winner two starts back, Venusienne rates the biggest threat to top spot and has run over today's trip before; a below-par effort when pulled up three starts back is the risk attached.

runners_data.name: Missus Beeton
runners_data.note: Consistent at OR 120 but her best form has come on Soft ground (two wins) and a good-going record of 10/15 suggests she can cope, though the stiffer test of 2m½f on quicker ground is a mild query.
runners_data.comment: Below-par when unplaced last time out, though the formbook shows back-to-back wins three and four starts back for Missus Beeton, who has run over today's trip and going before; needs to rediscover that better form.

runners_data.name: Billie Frechette
runners_data.note: Meade's five-year-old has placed in her last three outings on Good ground over 2m-2m6f; prominent style suits this setup and she's 59 days fresh, which counts as a minor watch point for fitness.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and runner-up three and four starts back, Billie Frechette also won five starts back and has run over today's trip and going before; the main risk is the 59-day gap since that run.

runners_data.name: Samba Train
runners_data.note: Three wins from seven on Good ground with Bolger's runner in excellent recent form (won last, OR 118); a genuine prominent type with a fine record at Galway distances and a claiming rider (Halford 7lb) to note.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and twice more in the past five starts, Samba Train boasts a strong scoring record and has run over today's trip and going before; question marks remain after a 79-day absence and finishes as low as sixth in between.

runners_data.name: Ardeen Joy
runners_data.note: Elliott-Kennedy combination is powerful and this mare won last time at 2m4f on Good ground; her 1W3P record on similar going, combined with Kennedy's tactical intelligence in big fields, makes her a serious player off OR 115.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but rates towards the bottom of this field on our figures, and a fall among her recent starts underlines the risk; has at least run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Splashing Out
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up type (one of the few) who won last time on Good over a shorter trip; Smithers 7lb claim helps with the weights and her ability to avoid the mid-pack congestion makes her profile interesting.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to end an otherwise workmanlike recent sequence, and has run over today's trip and going before, but Splashing Out steps back out after a 61-day absence which leaves a small query.

runners_data.name: Zahra Dodville
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with limited hurdle form but placed second last time on Good ground; naturally prominent but the redistribution squeeze may push her into a less comfortable position — Calum Hogan's 5lb claim is a compensating factor.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and a winner three starts back, Zahra Dodville arrives with a trainer among the yard's in-form performers and has run over today's trip and going before; a 67-day gap since is the only slight worry.

runners_data.name: Camlin Park
runners_data.note: A 114-day absence is the most significant flag here; won on Good over 2m2f so the trip and going are not concerns, but this layoff for McConnell's mare demands a fitness caveat in a field of this quality.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in each of its past two starts, Camlin Park rates bottom of this field on our figures and joins a yard currently out of form; a win three starts back is the only bright spot, but a 114-day layoff adds further doubt.

runners_data.name: Fratas
runners_data.note: Slevin partners this Joseph O'Brien-trained hold-up type who is one of the genuine closers in the race; OR 112 may underrate her if she gets a smooth run, but her recent form (pulled up, then 15th) needs to bounce back sharply.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last four starts, Fratas has been runner-up twice in that sequence and joins a trainer currently among the yard's in-form performers, having also run over today's trip and going before; consistency without going one better is the pattern to note.

runners_data.name: Wonderfulwonderful
runners_data.note: Four-year-old who is lightly raced over hurdles but won over Good ground on her reappearance; naturally prominent but in a field where her ORR 115 places her midfield competitively, trip extension to 2m½f is the unknown.
runners_data.comment: Fifth last time out, though Wonderfulwonderful won three starts back and has run over today's trip and going before; a yard currently out of form is the main concern heading into this deep field.

runners_data.name: Crohan Lady
runners_data.note: Won over 2m on Soft last time, and naturally races up with the pace — but with so many prominent horses in this field, she is unlikely to get her preferred forward berth; her 7/12 similar-going record is the key form angle.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and a winner three starts back, Crohan Lady has run over today's trip and going before, though a well-beaten ninth and eighth further back temper the overall picture.

runners_data.name: Cleopatra's Needle
runners_data.note: This mare has placed twice recently and won over Good in the past; she is a front-running type by preference but the overcrowded prominent group means she will likely find herself racing further back than ideal, limiting her chance.
runners_data.comment: Seventh last time out, but Cleopatra's Needle won two starts back and was runner-up in the two starts before that, and has run over today's trip and going before; back after just an 18-day break.

runners_data.name: Hillhead Runner
runners_data.note: Consistent in Good-ground handicaps but a string of moderate finishes (4-7-9-8-2) suggests she finds one or two too good at the business end; her natural forward style is compromised by the race shape here.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts, Hillhead Runner was fourth last time out, with a much stronger runner-up effort five starts back the highlight, and has run over today's trip and going before after a quick 19-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Two Pair
runners_data.note: Won at OR equivalent over 17f on Good ground; she is a positive mover who prefers to race prominently, but her most recent run (8th after a win) is a concern, and being mapped to midfield does not suit her proven pattern.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last time out, Two Pair does have a win two starts back and a runner-up effort further back in its favour, and has run over today's trip and going before; a 74-day gap since that below-par run adds to the questions.

runners_data.name: Simple Things
runners_data.note: Has placed twice over 2m4f on Good ground and is a genuine prominent type by style; however, being pushed back in this field means she races outside her comfort zone, and her 51-day absence for Dempsey adds a minor freshness question.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in its last five starts, Simple Things was fifth last time out after back-to-back runner-up efforts two and three starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before; needs to find more after a 51-day break.

runners_data.name: Astelia
runners_data.note: Remarkable record of eight seconds in recent outings without a win at OR 103; Fahey's mare is a model of consistency on Good ground but her inability to get her head in front at this level is the defining concern.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win despite three consecutive runner-up efforts, the latest coming last time out, Astelia has run over today's trip and going before, though the profile is patchier further back with an unplaced run and a seventh in its two starts before that.

runners_data.name: Bossy Bird
runners_data.note: Has placed twice on Good ground over 2m4f+ but the ⚠ fade flag is significant over this 2m½f trip; a natural prominent type, she carries the double disadvantage of likely midfield positioning and a known tendency to weaken in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but runner-up last time out, Bossy Bird otherwise has a modest recent record with back-to-back eighths further back, and has run over today's trip and going before; hard to fancy from a rating well down the field.

runners_data.name: Small Bucks
runners_data.note: Won 15 days ago over 2m2f on Good ground (OR 102, H style), making her freshness an asset; the ⚠ fade flag is a real concern stepping up to 2m½f, but her natural hold-up style is one of the few genuine closers in this field.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, though Small Bucks otherwise has a mixed record including a pulled-up run five starts back, and rates modestly on our figures; has run over today's trip and going before after a swift 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Sea Of Doubt
runners_data.note: Ran just one day ago, which is an extreme freshness flag and a potential welfare or fitness concern regardless of form; her form at similar going is excellent (15/15) with a 1W7P record, but that turnaround is almost impossible to ignore negatively.
runners_data.comment: Unseated last time out, though the form before that reads more solidly with alternating runner-up efforts, and Sea Of Doubt has run over today's trip and going before; a rapid turnaround of just a day since that unseated run adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Emesteraye
runners_data.note: Placed twice on Good (3rd at 2m and 2m1f recently) with no declared jockey listed; a hold-up type who will likely get a clean run from the back, but OR 100 and the quality of this field make her chances modest without an exceptional ride.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but third in both of its past two starts, Emesteraye has run over today's trip and going before and returns after a 27-day break; needs to find extra to go one better having missed out further back.

runners_data.name: Tingarran Express
runners_data.note: A nine-year-old with a win and a second on Good ground; naturally prominent but the redistribution cost is real at her age and OR 100 level, and 26 days since her last run means she arrives reasonably fresh without a jockey confirmed.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last time out, though Tingarran Express was runner-up two starts back and won five starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before; needs to bounce back from that below-par recent effort after a 26-day break.

runners_data.name: You Make Me Smile
runners_data.note: Three consecutive places on Good ground (2-3-2) make her consistent at OR 98; another prominent type by preference who is squeezed into midfield by this race shape, and without a listed jockey, she is hard to assess for tactical execution.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, You Make Me Smile has a modest recent record otherwise including a win four starts back, and has run over today's trip and going before; rates near the bottom of a large field on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: She's A Fine Wine is the one confirmed front-runner in a field of 23 and, critically, she faces no genuine rival for the lead — she will stride to the front unchallenged and dictate a sustainable, measured gallop over the 2m½f trip on Good ground. The bulk of the field — Crohan Lady, Cleopatra's Needle, Simple Things, Hillhead Runner, Two Pair and several others — are natural prominent racers who will be compressed into midfield because there simply is not room for them all to race where they want; this crowding will create a dense, scrappy mid-race group and leave She's A Fine Wine with a rare luxury of space and rhythm. Samba Train, Billie Frechette, Ardeen Joy and Venusienne are the highest-rated genuine prominent types who are most likely to actually secure a handy position behind the leader, giving them the clearest sight of the winner coming down the hill. With one horse controlling a controlled tempo and a legitimate class edge at OR 125, this race shape strongly favours horses that can track the leader in the first four or five — those who get a clean, uninterrupted passage from the front of the main pack will have the decisive advantage, making patient front-to-mid profiles the dominant winning profile today.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: She's A Fine Wine Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If She's A Fine Wine bowls along uncontested and the moderate pace produces a test of class and jumping rather than stamina.
scenarios.body: She's A Fine Wine controls every yard from an uncontested lead on Good ground, the field fans out below her, and her OR 125 combined with excellent recent form (two wins from last two) make her impossible to peg back if she retains her fluency.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If She's A Fine Wine's lead is sufficient to stretch the pack but one of the genuine prominent types holds a perfect position three to four lengths off the pace and picks her off at the last.
scenarios.body: Ardeen Joy, Samba Train or Venusienne, all capable of travelling smoothly in the slipstream of the leader, emerge from a tightly contested battle in the chasing group to challenge from the second-last hurdle, with the winner being the one who gets an unobstructed run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closer Gets Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just fast enough to tie up the prominent brigade and a hold-up type threads through a tiring pack late on.
scenarios.body: Splashing Out or Fratas, genuine hold-up horses, are given a masterclass steer wide of the congestion that will inevitably form from so many redistributed prominent types jostling for space, and arrive with a late rattle.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pack Implodes, Outsider Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the dense mid-race traffic causes fallers or interference that bunches the field, allowing a lightly regarded runner to emerge from the carnage.
scenarios.body: With 23 runners over hurdles on Good ground, traffic incidents are plausible; a runner like Zahra Dodville or Simple Things, capable of sitting just off the worst of the scrimmage, could benefit if the fancied mid-pack horses are baulked or hampered.

watchPoints.text: Sea Of Doubt ran just one day ago — connections must be watched in the parade ring for any signs of fatigue or stiffness, and any reported setback would immediately remove her from contention.

With 23 runners over hurdles, the first and second flight will be congested as the redistributed prominent types jostle for position — watch for Hillhead Runner, Two Pair and Bossy Bird specifically, all natural forward movers likely to meet interference.

She's A Fine Wine (De Bromhead) should be monitored in the pre-race; if she is reported to be sweating or edgy, her ability to produce her trademark front-running effectiveness may be compromised in a field that could overrun her at the first if she misses a beat.

Camlin Park's 114-day layoff is the longest in the field — watch her in the early market moves and pre-race reports; if she is unconsidered in betting, the fitness angle is likely priced in, but a stable whisper either way would be significant.

Ardeen Joy (Kennedy) and Samba Train (Halford 7lb) are the two prominent-style horses most likely to secure a position directly behind She's A Fine Wine — watch how quickly each of them travels to the front group at the start, as that positioning will be decisive.

races.name: Tote Galway Plate (Handicap Steeplechase) (Grade 3)

runners_data.name: Senecia
runners_data.note: OR 153, won last time on good ground over similar trip, 79 days off, blinkered — travels prominently and Paul Barry's typical front-end tactics make him a genuine early challenger to Three Card Brag's lead; good-ground form is solid.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, though two of his last five starts ended pulled up. Fresh for 79 days, he tops our figures here and rates the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Three Card Brag
runners_data.note: The confirmed sole front-runner here, uncontested lead is his to take — good-ground record is mixed (7/15) but he won over this trip and course conditions suit a front-running setup; Kevin Healy's 7lb claim is a significant weight advantage and could be decisive if he dictates throughout.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and has run over today's trip and going before, rating close behind the top-rated runner on our figures. The two starts before that were well beaten, the one blot on an otherwise solid profile.

runners_data.name: Funiculi Funicula
runners_data.note: Paul Townend in the plate is immediately significant; unbeaten in two over fences on good or good-to-firm, this lightly-raced six-year-old has a prominent style and the form figures 211 suggest a horse in strong form — distance step up to 2m6½f is the only query.
runners_data.comment: Placed in each of his last four starts, winning last time out, and the time before that too, with a second and third further back. Has run over today's going before, though 89 days off is the concern.

runners_data.name: Gorgeous Tom
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner who has shown his best form on good ground (win and placed), though recent form on softer has been modest; Patrick O'Brien's 5lb claim helps on the weight, but the 109-day absence and soft-ground pattern of recent runs tempers enthusiasm.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last four starts, though he was a second four starts back and has run over today's trip and going before. A 109-day break and a rating above his official mark are the main concerns.

runners_data.name: Will The Wise
runners_data.note: Winner of his last two, including on soft and good, and fitted with a tongue-tie — Cromwell/Donoghue combination is in fine form; races prominently and 110 days off fresh, which suits horses who want to be handy rather than warm up into a race.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out, and again five starts back, with a runner-up effort in between and experience over today's trip and going. A 110-day layoff and a stable on just 5% (2 from 38) lately temper the claims.

runners_data.name: Jesse Evans
runners_data.note: Outstanding good-ground profile — 15/15 runs on similar conditions with four wins and 11 placings is an exceptional stat; races prominently, Sam Ewing takes over, and the form string 225-31 shows consistency at this level; likely sits just off Three Card Brag.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and has otherwise raced consistently, with only a fifth three starts back interrupting a run of places. Quick to return after 58 days, with experience over today's trip and going, and rated above his official mark — a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Ol Man Dingle
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie and breast-girth fitted; won on good ground 44 days ago and races prominently — relatively fresh, course-appropriate surface, and a horse progressing through OR 145; Ricky Doyle has taken off the tongue-tie previously when winning.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and was third two starts back, though the form dips further back with a seventh and an unplaced run among the finishes. Has run over today's trip and going before and is rated on a par with his official mark after 44 days off.

runners_data.name: Perceval Legallois
runners_data.note: Only 19 days since last run (placed second on good ground), Harry Cobden booked — tongue-tie fitted and recent form includes a win at Galway; has a habit of unseating and pulling up, however, and that jumping fragility in a 25-runner field is a real risk.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, though runner-up last time out and has run over today's trip and going before. The formline turns patchy further back, including a pulled up and an unseated rider, and a stable on just 5% adds to the concerns.

runners_data.name: Downmexicoway
runners_data.note: Won last two on good-to-yielding/good ground and placed just behind that; 141-day absence is the chief concern for De Bromhead, who fires horses back fresh but this is a long layoff; genuine two-and-a-half mile plus performer with sound jumping.
runners_data.comment: A modest fourth last time out, though the form claims are solid further back with two wins and a second among the last five. Has run over today's going before, though a lengthy 141-day absence is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Diamond
runners_data.note: True hold-up type, one of the few genuine ones in this field; six-year-old who finished second on good ground over 23f last time, shaped with ability; Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim is a bonus but the horse has shown only flashes — a genuinely patient ride could unlock him.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts but rated well above his official mark, suggesting more ability than the bare results show. Has run over today's trip and going before, though unplaced last time out, with the form cooling since a second five starts back.

runners_data.name: Nowwhatdoyouthink
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes a mount he can be expected to position prominently from the off — three wins on good ground in last four starts on that surface speaks for itself; OR 142, progressive at seven, and the tongue-tie has been a constant positive.
runners_data.comment: Consistency itself, placed in every one of his last five starts including a third last time out, with two wins in that sequence. Has run over today's trip and going before and rates a touch above his official mark, though 92 days off is a small concern.

runners_data.name: Reverend Hubert
runners_data.note: One of only two genuinely natural hold-up horses in the field alongside Rocky's Diamond; OR 142 but the going figures (14/15 on good) are exceptional — four wins from those starts — and Phillip Enright knows this horse well; needs the pace to lift in the final mile to deliver his challenge.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and again three starts back, with the sequence otherwise mixed including an unplaced run four starts back. Quick to reappear on a 19-day turnaround, has run over today's trip and going before, and edges a touch clear of his official mark.

runners_data.name: Maxxum
runners_data.note: A true prominent racer by nature but shuffled back in the mapping given the traffic of front-end types; Danny Gilligan takes the ride and the form last time (0 from 10 over 24f on good) was poor — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects the compromised position he's likely to occupy.
runners_data.comment: Unplaced last time out, though that follows a useful sequence including a win three starts back and two thirds further back. Has run over today's trip and going before, with 65 days off since that below-par effort.

runners_data.name: Nouvotic
runners_data.note: Holds four wins in nine good-ground starts and was placed second most recently, so form and going are perfectly aligned; naturally wants to race prominently but Mike O'Connor will be unable to secure that position with so many front-end types — the forced-back role genuinely compromises his chance (STYLE_FIT 0.91).
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts and runner-up last time out reads well, but our figures only line him up with his official mark, some way behind the leading contenders here. Has run over today's trip and going before, fit again after 26 days.

runners_data.name: Buddy One
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse on a poor run of form — 66P40 is not encouraging and the 21-day turnaround suggests connections are keeping him busy rather than peaking him; trip and going are acceptable but recent evidence is against him.
runners_data.comment: Without a win in his last five starts and up against it on recent form figures, including a pulled up three starts back. Has run over today's trip and going before, quick to reappear after 21 days, and is rated well above his official mark despite that profile.

runners_data.name: King Alexander
runners_data.note: Daniel King rides for Mullins; won over 20f on heavy-to-soft and has placed on good, but the natural prominence means he'll struggle to get a clear run in this pack — STYLE_FIT 0.90 reflects the squeeze he'll face racing outside his ideal position.

runners_data.name: King Of Kingsfield
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's runner fitted with tongue-tie and breast-girth; won over 18f on good last time 27 days ago but the step up to 2m6½f in a 25-runner field is a significant ask, and a hold-up horse in a compressed midfield faces a tough afternoon.
runners_data.comment: A modest fifth last time out, and the form is patchy further back, including a pulled up four starts back, though he won five starts back. Has run over today's going before and is rated a few pounds above his official mark after 27 days off.

runners_data.name: Spread Boss Ted
runners_data.note: Brian Hayes rides for Mullins; one win from 12 on good ground is a concern for the surface, and while naturally prominent the redistribution to midfield reflects how crowded the early order will be — STYLE_FIT 0.90 signals the challenge of executing in this field.

runners_data.name: Solitary Man
runners_data.note: Won last time over 26f on good ground — the trip and surface are right; Aidan Kelly rides for Bolger and the horse has four wins from 11 on good, which is a meaningful stat; but a naturally prominent racer forced further back in this field faces a compromised passage.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and again three starts back, with two fourths and a ninth further back rounding out a modest overall picture. Has run over today's trip and going before, but our figures rate him only 21st of 25 here, marginally below his official mark.

runners_data.name: Ballygunner Castle
runners_data.note: Danny Mullins takes a Mullins-trained runner who has placed on good ground twice; seven-year-old over fences with a mixed form string — naturally prominent but banished to the midfield in the mapping, and the STYLE_FIT concern (0.92) is real in a field this deep.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last four starts, fourth last time out with a fall and two runner-up efforts further back. Has run over today's trip and going before, with 89 days off and a rating a couple of pounds above his official mark.

runners_data.name: Barry Lyndon
runners_data.note: Won last time over 24f on good ground 88 days ago, tongue-tie and breast-girth fitted — the form and going work, and J J Slevin is an obvious booking upgrade; a true prominent horse whose natural position is compromised here (STYLE_FIT 0.93) but the horse may have enough class to overcome it.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out, and again five starts back, but the finishes in between were modest and our figures now place him only 23rd of 25, a few pounds below his official mark. Has run over today's trip and going before after 88 days off.

runners_data.name: Conyers Hill
runners_data.note: Two recent second-place finishes on good ground show he's consistent; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim is a weight advantage; fitted with cheekpieces and historically holds up, suggesting he might find a cleaner passage from further back than many of the other redistributed prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last five starts, though runner-up last time out, and again two starts back, before a fifth, a fall and a fourth further back. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated a couple of pounds above his official mark after 65 days off.

runners_data.name: Jalila Moriviere
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained seven-year-old with a tongue-tie; three placings in five good-ground runs but not a winner on the surface — naturally prominent but mapped to midfield given the traffic; STYLE_FIT 0.92 applies and the form to date hasn't included a win at this level.

runners_data.name: Boston Rover
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins going into the current campaign, now 5/26f on good last time — the drop in form may reflect the trip and company rather than the horse deteriorating; naturally prominent, Gordon Elliott runner forced back, STYLE_FIT 0.90 — but the winning sequence earlier in the year suggests raw ability.
runners_data.comment: Three wins on the spin further back catch the eye, but that sequence ended with a pulled up two starts back, and a modest fifth last time out. Has run over today's trip and going before, though rated bottom of the field here, marginally below his official mark.

runners_data.note: 116-day absence is the longest in the field; form on soft has been moderate (three placings, no win) and the going is different here, which is uncertain; naturally prominent but the combination of long layoff and STYLE_FIT concern (0.93) makes this a difficult horse to assess confidently.
runners_data.comment: A third last time out heads a modest recent sequence that includes a win four starts back among three below-par efforts. Has run over today's trip and going before, rated a few pounds above her official mark after a lengthy 116-day absence.

races.paceDynamic: Three Card Brag is the confirmed front-runner and, critically, faces no serious rival for the lead in a field where the majority of the 25 runners are prominent or mid-division types — meaning the early pace is likely to be measured and controlled rather than pressurised. On good ground over 2m6½f at Galway, a single uncontested leader sets a rhythm that rewards horses travelling smoothly just off the pace and punishes those who expend energy fighting for position early. The bulk of the field — Nouvotic, Maxxum, Spread Boss Ted, King Alexander, Solitary Man, Ballygunner Castle, Barry Lyndon, Conyers Hill, Jalila Moriviere, Boston Rover and Ballybawn Belter — are genuine prominent types who cannot all hold their natural position and will be forced to settle further back than ideal, compressing the midfield and creating traffic complications. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can be accommodated at the head of affairs; among those most likely to secure an early position close to Three Card Brag are Senecia, Funiculi Funicula, Jesse Evans, Will The Wise and Nowwhatdoyouthink, who have both the profile and connections to press forward. The tactical verdict is clear: a controlled, single-paced gallop on good ground over this trip favours prominent-to-handy racers who can track the leader, jump fluently and produce a sustained finish — horses held up deep will face the double problem of traffic and a pace that never truly collapses the field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Three Card Brag sets a sustainable tempo unchallenged and the prominent chasers track smoothly before the last.
scenarios.body: Three Card Brag dictates a fair clip but not a gruelling one, and the horses positioned just behind — Jesse Evans, Nowwhatdoyouthink, Senecia — are delivered with a clean run to challenge from the second-last fence; good ground rewards the accurate jumper who travels through the race rather than groping for position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Three Card Brag goes very steady early, the compressed midfield shuffles, and a strong stayer sweeps through in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: A slow tempo with a wall of horses in behind creates a sprint-finish scenario over the last two fences, benefiting strong gallopers who have been conserving energy from well off the pace; Reverend Hubert and Rocky's Diamond, genuine hold-up types, would be the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Front Runner Lands
scenarios.trigger: If Three Card Brag, supported by Kevin Healy, builds the gallop from halfway and kicks clear before the second-last to make all.
scenarios.body: A genuine front-runner who is uncontested and gets into a rhythm on good ground can be very hard to collar over this distance when connections commit early; horses who travel prominently and jump well — Funiculi Funicula and Perceval Legallois — are best placed to give chase, but a dominant display from Three Card Brag at a true gallop could see the field strung out.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Longshot Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield causes widespread interference at a crucial fence and a lightly-weighted, adaptable stayer picks through the wreckage.
scenarios.body: With 25 runners and a bulging midfield of displaced prominent types, incident at a fence — particularly down the back stretch — could open gaps for a horse carrying less weight and racing with fresh legs; Ol Man Dingle and Downmexicoway, both lower-weighted and capable on good ground, have the profile to capitalise on disruption ahead of them.

races.paceDynamic: Sunny South West is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure identified to chase him down, he is likely to control tempo from the front in a 21-runner field over 1m4f on yielding ground at Galway. The pace he sets is likely to be honest but sustainable — he has multiple front-running wins to his name and Derek O'Connor will not be wasteful — meaning the race will be run at a measured gallop that keeps the field strung out without burning off the leaders. This favours prominent racers who can track the pace from close range and quicken at the business end, rather than deep hold-up horses who will find 21 runners and a true-run mile-and-a-half difficult to make up from the rear. The field contains more prominent and front-running types than the map can accommodate: Nakassama, Hopes Are High, and Daddy Long Legs are the most credible challengers to actually secure a position on the pace behind Sunny South West, with redistributed hold-up types Eyeeye and Believe Again unlikely to obtain their natural rear-of-field berth easily in a race this size.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sunny South West Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Sunny South West takes his customary lead and sets a fair but uncontested gallop, the race is run to suit prominent closers who track within three lengths.
scenarios.body: Sunny South West dictates from the front with Derek O'Connor riding to his strengths, and horses settled just off the pace — able to respond once the field strings out on the Galway straight — are handed the ideal conditions; Daddy Long Legs and Glowing Account, both patient prominently-raced types from the powerful Mullins yard with proven form in similar conditions, fit this profile precisely.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Front Holds
scenarios.trigger: If the even gallop proves easier than expected on yielding ground and Sunny South West is never headed, he conserves enough to hold on.
scenarios.body: With a light weight of competition for the lead and 21 runners creating traffic problems for those off the pace, Sunny South West could simply pinch a lead he is never asked to surrender until too late; his trainer Edward Power has shown good form over the festival and the horse's record of five wins and five places from nine runs on similar going underlines his suitability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves genuinely testing on the yielding ground and the leaders tie up in the straight, horses settled in mid-division who travel well through the race emerge late.
scenarios.body: Hopes Are High and Nakassama, though mapped to midfield due to redistribution rather than natural inclination, each carry strong form in similar going and distances and could pick up the pieces if the front rank fades; a genuinely run race over this trip on yielding ground does not entirely close the door on well-handicapped types from this position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field and backmarkers find a clear passage in the straight, deep hold-up horses get home late.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires both a strong gallop and a gap through 21 runners — a low-probability conjunction at Galway over this trip — but Silas Marner and Believe Again have placed form at distance and would not be without a shout if it materialised; the congested nature of the field and the redistribution of natural hold-up types into midfield make this the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Can Happen runs just 2 days after her last outing — monitor for any vet or trainer update before the off, as the turnaround is extremely short for a 6-year-old in a competitive 21-runner field.
Galileo Springs has no jockey listed in the racecard data — confirm the ride is taken before assessing her chance, as a late jockey booking or withdrawal could alter the race shape.

Nakassama and Hopes Are High are natural prominent racers who cannot both get their preferred positions in a field this size — watch the early exchanges to see who gets outpaced or drops back, as the one who does will be racing out of role for the remainder.

Sunny South West is tagged STYLE_FIT=0.91, indicating he may be racing slightly out of role himself despite being the confirmed pace-setter — if he is pushed off his natural rhythm early in a 21-runner field, the tempo could become ragged.
Silas Marner returns from 411 days off and Glowing Account from 943 days — both require significant fitness assumptions; watch the market moves on these two to gauge stable confidence.

runners_data.name: Moonlit Sun

runners_data.comment: Won last time out and third before that, Moonlit Sun has a tidy if brief recent formline, but our figures rate her modestly in this field, and she has run over today's trip and going before from draw 8.

runners_data.name: God Of Power
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery trains and rides, giving him full tactical control; placed twice in five recent starts over a mile on good ground and the extra half-furlong should be within range, though a 9-of-10 record without a win on similar going is a mild caution.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, God Of Power was runner-up two starts back and won three starts back, though a well-beaten ninth four starts back shows some inconsistency; has run over today's trip and going before from draw 13.

runners_data.name: Kirkland Sioux
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's yard is in strong 14-day form (16/67) and Declan McDonogh takes over on a horse who has won back-to-back over a mile on good — the step to 9.5f on yielding looks a natural next move and this runner has serious claims.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins last time out and two starts back stand out, but Kirkland Sioux otherwise has a modest record and rates near the bottom of this field on our figures despite a strong yard and a swift 10-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Amenita
runners_data.note: Dermot Weld's runner won last time over a mile on good but is a natural front-rank horse pushed back on the map because of field congestion up front — Reese Holohan's 7lb claim helps compensate, and the horse's last win came over the same trip on the same type of ground.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out but well beaten before that, Amenita sits bottom of this field on our figures and has run over today's trip before, though a 58-day break since her last outing adds to the queries.

runners_data.name: Johnny Soda
runners_data.note: Three wins from nine starts on soft or good-to-soft makes this an excellent ground fit; races prominently and has won over 8f on soft twice, with the extra distance looking manageable for a horse that stays well — strong contender in any scenario where the front group is not excessively disrupted.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins last time out and two starts back headline a strong recent record for Johnny Soda, who also won five starts back and has run over today's trip and going before from draw 4; a seventh and fifth in between are the only blots.

runners_data.name: Krasimir
runners_data.note: Six consecutive placed efforts without a win show consistency but also a vulnerability to being run out of it; Gary Lyons sends this one with a tongue-tie, and while he handles good ground well, being a natural prominent racer unable to get that berth in this field is a genuine setback.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out to cap a consistent run never worse than third, Krasimir rates a big threat on our figures and has run over today's trip and going before from draw 3; stepping up to face this field's best is the risk attached.

runners_data.name: Monvoe
runners_data.note: Three wins from 13 starts with a promising recent sequence of 1-1-2, but recorded a 9th on good over 9f last time out suggesting the extra distance is not a certainty; W.J. Lee has to manage being pushed back from his preferred position, which undermines what has previously been a front-running profile.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten last time out, though a winner two starts back, runner-up three starts back and a winner again four starts back is a strong recent record. Has run over today's trip and going before from draw 12, and that below-par latest run is the query.

runners_data.name: Time Bender
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good but three of his last four runs produced finishes of 5th or 6th; this is a horse whose one win came comfortably at a shorter trip, and being shuffled off a prominent position makes a repeat of that form here harder to achieve on yielding ground.

runners_data.name: Loch Gamhna

runners_data.name: Monoceros

runners_data.comment: Yet to win but competitive throughout, with a runner-up effort three starts back, Minella Rockett rates among the leading dangers on our figures and has run over today's trip and going before from draw 11; a fifth last time out is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Golddream
runners_data.note: David Marnane's runner has not won on good or soft in five attempts (0W/1P), and while Luke McAteer takes the ride, this is a natural front-runner who cannot get to the front in this field — the form figures of 5-5-3-1-6 show one bright spot but insufficient evidence of consistent ability at this level.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back fifths in its past two starts leave Golddream with work to do, though a win four starts back shows the ability is there, and it has run over today's trip and going before from draw 9; hard to trust on this evidence alone.

races.paceDynamic: Mayflower is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner field and looks set to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on yielding ground at Galway, with no natural rival likely to seriously pressure her early. The pace she sets will be measured rather than frantic, creating a controlled tempo that plays into the hands of prominent racers travelling just off her shoulder — horses like Kirkland Sioux, Johnny Soda and Moonlit Sun, all of whom have genuine placed-to-win form racing handy. This field is saturated with prominent-type runners: Amenita, Krasimir, Monvoe, Time Bender, Minella Rockett and Golddream are all natural front-rank horses who cannot all occupy their preferred position, meaning several will be shuffled back involuntarily and will not be racing in their comfort zone. The race shape strongly favours horses who can sit second or third without fuss and kick off a genuine gallop — a prominent, front-rank profile in an uncontested but not truly strong-pace scenario is the profile to find.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mayflower Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Mayflower leads at a fair but unforced gallop and the prominent stalkers travel smoothly just off her through the home straight.
scenarios.body: Kirkland Sioux, Moonlit Sun and Johnny Soda are all proven at the trip and distance, racing handily off a single honest front-runner on ground they handle; the moderate gallop allows them to settle and produce a genuine turn-of-foot entering the final furlong. Prominent types who have won over 8f on good or soft dominate this shape, and the Galway straight rewards a well-timed challenge from just off the pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Hold Steady, Kick Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the middle portion of the race sees Mayflower gradually overtaken and the genuine prominent pair — Kirkland Sioux and Johnny Soda — move to the front two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: Kirkland Sioux has won back-to-back over a mile on good ground and steps up in trip for the first time, while Johnny Soda has three wins in ten starts with a strong record on soft ground, suggesting both have the engine to grind it out on yielding. With redistributed runners unable to reproduce their front-running form from further back, these two are the most likely to dominate a two-horse duel.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Redistributed Runners Find Feet
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is slow enough that several of the demoted prominent types — Krasimir, Monvoe or Amenita — manage to push forward and compete at the head of the field despite their mapped position.
scenarios.body: Krasimir has run six consecutive placed efforts and handles this ground, while Monvoe has three wins from 13 starts and won over 8f on good; if the race compresses and creates space at the front, either could recover their natural position. However, this scenario carries a meaningful discount because it relies on riders overcoming the race shape rather than working with it.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops into a rough, crowded affair with a pace collapse late, allowing Monoceros or Loch Gamhna to deliver from the rear.
scenarios.body: Monoceros has placed in 3 of 6 on good or soft and could theoretically benefit from a messy finish in a big field, while Loch Gamhna has shown stamina form over longer trips. This is a low-probability shape because neither hold-up runner has strong enough form figures to overcome the structural advantage of the prominent profile in this race.

watchPoints.text: Kirkland Sioux is the most dangerous horse in the race — back-to-back wins over a mile for an in-form O'Brien yard, Declan McDonogh booked, and a natural step up to 9.5f on ground he acts on; watch whether he settles smoothly just off Mayflower.

Johnny Soda has three wins on soft or good-to-soft going and a prominent racing style that suits this scenario exactly — if he travels fluently in the first three, he is a serious threat to everything in the straight.

The number of prominent-type runners redistributed to midfield (Amenita, Krasimir, Monvoe, Time Bender, Minella Rockett, Golddream) creates a risk of a crowded, scrappy middle section as riders attempt to recover lost ground — watch for interference or traffic issues around the half-mile marker.

Mayflower has not run for 66 days and is stepping up in trip — if she fades earlier than expected in the straight rather than being overtaken cleanly, it could cause interference to the prominent stalkers immediately behind her.

Amenita (D.K. Weld, Reese Holohan 7lb claim) is technically OR=85 with a win last time on the same type of ground — if the race somehow compresses and she recovers her natural position, the form and jockey allowance combination makes her a live outsider to note.
